findings.title: Hard-coded database URL with password
findings.detail: A credential is written in the configuration file, readable by anything that can read the file and copied into backups and dotfile repositories.
findings.fix: Move it to the environment or a secret store and reference it (for example ${SERVER_TOKEN}); then rotate it, since it has been on disk.

findings.title: Hard-coded GitHub token
findings.detail: A credential is written in the configuration file, readable by anything that can read the file and copied into backups and dotfile repositories.
findings.fix: Move it to the environment or a secret store and reference it (for example ${GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}); then rotate it, since it has been on disk.

findings.title: Hard-coded Slack token
findings.detail: A credential is written in the configuration file, readable by anything that can read the file and copied into backups and dotfile repositories.
findings.fix: Move it to the environment or a secret store and reference it (for example ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}); then rotate it, since it has been on disk.

findings.title: Hard-coded Anthropic API key
findings.detail: The Authorization header holds a literal credential.
findings.fix: Reference it from the environment and rotate it.

findings.title: Remote server over plain HTTP
findings.detail: Requests, results and any credential travel unencrypted and can be read or changed on the network.

findings.title: Access to the whole filesystem
findings.detail: The server is given the filesystem root: every file the user can read (keys, browser profiles, other projects) is in reach of the agent and of anything that injects instructions into it.
findings.fix: Give the server only the directories it needs, for example the project directory.

findings.title: Server fetched from a repository or URL at start
findings.detail: The code that runs is whatever the repository or URL holds at launch time, outside any registry's checks and without a pinned release.
findings.fix: Use a published release pinned to an exact version (or a commit hash).

findings.title: Server launched by a script downloaded at start
findings.detail: Whatever the URL serves at launch time runs with the user's rights; it can change at any time without notice.
findings.fix: Install a pinned release and run it directly.

findings.title: Credential embedded in the server URL
findings.detail: The URL itself grants access (path segment 3 (uuid), query user_id (token query key)). Anyone who sees it can use the server: it is copied into logs, process lists, shell history, screenshots and support tickets.
findings.fix: Rotate the URL with the provider if it has been shared, keep the file private, and prefer a provider option that authenticates with a header referenced from the environment.

findings.title: Credential embedded in the server URL
findings.detail: The URL itself grants access (path segment 2 (high-entropy)). Anyone who sees it can use the server: it is copied into logs, process lists, shell history, screenshots and support tickets.
findings.fix: Rotate the URL with the provider if it has been shared, keep the file private, and prefer a provider option that authenticates with a header referenced from the environment.

findings.title: Credential embedded in the server URL
findings.detail: The URL itself grants access (query api_key (token query key)). Anyone who sees it can use the server: it is copied into logs, process lists, shell history, screenshots and support tickets.
findings.fix: Rotate the URL with the provider if it has been shared, keep the file private, and prefer a provider option that authenticates with a header referenced from the environment.

findings.title: Literal value in secret-named field X-API-Key
findings.detail: The field's name says it holds a credential, and its value is written in the file rather than referenced.
findings.fix: Reference it from the environment (for example ${X_API_KEY}) and rotate it.

findings.title: Remote server with no credential configured
findings.detail: No Authorization or API-key header is configured. The client may still sign in with OAuth when it connects; if it does not, anyone who can reach the URL can use the server's tools.
findings.fix: Confirm the server requires authentication (OAuth or a header referenced from the environment).

findings.title: Server runs with the host network (container)
findings.detail: The server can reach far more than its tools need, which widens what a compromised or manipulated server can do.
findings.fix: Grant only the access the server needs (for Deno, --allow-net=<hosts>; for containers, a dedicated network).

findings.title: Unpinned server version
findings.detail: Each launch may run a different release, including a compromised one, without any change to this file.
findings.fix: Pin the image by digest (image@sha256:…) or at least an exact version tag.

findings.title: Unpinned server version
findings.detail: Each launch may run a different release, including a compromised one, without any change to this file.
findings.fix: Pin an exact version, for example example/github-mcp@1.2.3 (with its scope), and update it deliberately.

findings.title: Access to the whole home directory
findings.detail: The home directory holds SSH keys, cloud credentials, shell history and browser data.
findings.fix: Give the server only the directories it needs.

findings.title: Server pinned to a moving tag (latest)
findings.detail: Each launch may run a different release, including a compromised one, without any change to this file.
findings.fix: Pin an exact version (name==1.2.3) and update it deliberately.

findings.title: Server runs with all permissions (Deno)
findings.detail: The server can reach far more than its tools need, which widens what a compromised or manipulated server can do.
findings.fix: Grant only the access the server needs (for Deno, --allow-net=<hosts>; for containers, a dedicated network).

findings.title: Launched through Sievant
findings.detail: This server already runs behind `sievant proxy`: its calls pass Sievant's guardrails.

notes: Tool descriptions, and the resources and prompts each server offers, were not checked: that needs starting the servers (sievant scan --inspect-tools, which runs them).
